brief: A utensil holder with two bins that is waterproof and dishwasher safe.

requirements.evidence: Two adjacent full bases (piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full) each with a full-depth bin (bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full), dressed with spoon, fork and knife props standing in the bins; capped and joint-locked, check_build ok, meshClash clear.

Configurator checks fit/collisions only and knows nothing about materials or waterproofing; parts are 3D-printed in a user-chosen material. Solid (non-drained) bins were chosen so the shape holds utensils without drain holes, but waterproofing cannot be claimed.
Dishwasher/heat safety depends on the printed material, which the configurator does not know or verify; cannot be claimed from this build.

finish.summary: Built a two-bin utensil holder: two joined hex bases with solid full-depth bins, capped open faces and locked joints, staged with spoon/fork/knife props. Waterproof and dishwasher-safe cannot be met or verified here — they depend on the 3D-print material the user chooses, which the configurator does not assess — so those are reported unmet; solid bins were used to avoid drain holes.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
